Consult Summary:
- 3 days of acute diarrhea (4–5/day) with mild abdominal pain, one episode of vomiting, possible low-grade fever, and preserved oral intake; no blood or mucus; clinician judged not dehydrated; conservative management advised for likely self-limited gastroenteritis.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Diarrhea.
- Onset/duration: ~3 days.
- Frequency/character: 4–5 bowel movements/day; consistency varies by time of day from loose to watery.
- Associated symptoms: Mild abdominal pain; one episode of vomiting; reduced appetite; able to drink fluids; “maybe a little” fever.
- Pertinent negatives: No blood in stool; no mucus.
- Exposures: No recent travel; no suspicious/“dodgy” foods reported.
- Prior episodes: Has had similar episodes at times after certain foods or travel (none currently).
- Treatments tried: None for diarrhea or abdominal pain.
- Additional unclear statement: Patient said, “Mostly it’s been dry and red” — context unclear; patient denied blood in stool.

Past Medical History:
- Asthma: Patient reports prior history and believes he still has it; no recent exacerbations mentioned.

Medications:
- Asthma inhaler reported as “Laxepro/Lexapro,” yellow device (medication identity unclear) — dose/route/frequency not documented. Conflict noted: “Lexapro” is typically escitalopram (oral SSRI), but patient describes an inhaler.
- OTC medications: None currently for this illness.
- Allergies: No known allergies.

Social History:
- Travel: None recently.
- Diet: No unusual foods reported before onset.
- Other social history: Not recorded.

Family History:
- Father: Hypertension; died of bowel cancer at age 62 (10 years ago).

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Not recorded.
- General (video assessment): Clinician stated patient appears not dehydrated.
- Other systems: Not recorded.

Investigations:
- None performed at this visit.
- Plan for stool testing if diarrhea persists beyond 1 week or if blood appears in stool (per clinician advice).

Assessment & Plan:
- Overall Impression:
  - Acute self-limited gastroenteritis, most consistent with viral etiology given short duration, moderate frequency, brief vomiting, possible low-grade fever, and lack of blood/mucus; patient remains able to maintain hydration.

- DDx Integration (brief):
  - Acute viral gastroenteritis: Supports — 3-day course, loose/watery stools, one vomit, possible low-grade fever, preserved hydration; Opposes — no identified sick contacts.
  - Acute bacterial gastroenteritis/foodborne illness: Supports — acute watery diarrhea with mild pain; Opposes — no blood/mucus, no clear food exposure or travel.
  - Medication-induced diarrhea (e.g., SSRI): Low likelihood; Supports — “Lexapro” mentioned; Opposes — patient describes an inhaler (medication identity unclear) and no recent med change. Conflict noted.

- Issue 1: Acute diarrhea/gastroenteritis
  - Plan:
    - Hydration: Continue ample oral fluids; consider oral rehydration salts (Dioralyte) OTC — dose not documented.
    - Diet: “Soft” easily digested foods (e.g., crackers, toast, jam); avoid meat, fish, eggs, and milk while symptomatic. Yoghurt is acceptable (probiotic). Progress to boiled/mashed vegetables; once diarrhea-free for ~48 hours, gradually reintroduce meat/eggs/fish.
    - Monitoring/red flags: Seek care if frequency increases significantly. Conflict noted: clinician first stated “>8/day” is concerning; later stated “6–8/day” may indicate dehydration and need for hospital evaluation.
    - Return/Follow-up: If diarrhea persists beyond 1 week or if any blood appears, submit a stool sample for evaluation and re-contact clinician. Return earlier for signs of dehydration (e.g., worsening thirst, dizziness, reduced urine), inability to keep fluids down, high fever, or severe abdominal pain.
    - No antimicrobial therapy or antidiarrheals initiated during this visit per transcript.

- Issue 2: Asthma; unclear current inhaler
  - Plan:
    - Medication reconciliation needed to confirm exact inhaler name and regimen; verify at next contact.

- Issue 3: Family history of colorectal cancer (father at 62)
  - Plan:
    - Documented today; no actions discussed during this consult.

- General plan items:
  - Patient advised that visit notes and instructions will be available in the app for review.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: No vitals; limited ROS; medication list and dosing incomplete; vaccination status and recent antibiotic use not discussed; stool characteristics beyond consistency (odor/volume) not described.
- Conflicts: Threshold for concerning stool frequency given as “>8/day” vs “6–8/day” during the same consult; medication identity “Laxepro/Lexapro” unclear (inhaler vs oral SSRI).
- Unclear statement: “Mostly it’s been dry and red” — context not established; patient denied blood in stool.
- Transcript quality: One unclear patient remark required repetition; otherwise understandable.
